newsitem.title: UK: Redland sees continued Europe weakness.
newsitem.headline: Redland sees continued Europe weakness.

text.p: Redland Plc, the building materials group, said on Thursday it expected continued sluggishness in Europe, after reporting pre-exceptional 1996 profits of 259 million pounds ($421.8 million).

Profits fell from last year's 273.2 million and were knocked back even more sharply to 200.9 million, after taking account of a one-off 58 million hit. On the outlook, Robert Napier, chief executive, said "In general European roofing markets are expected to remain weak with overall volumes similar to those in 1996." French aggregate demand is seen remaining depressed and British demand up modestly.

Napier added that British aggregate selling prices were firm after price rises and said the U.S market conditions "remain strong and management actions continue to yield the expected performance improvements."

The chief summed up "Following the major strategic reorganisation successfully completed last year, the group is now in a good posiiton to generate substantially improved cash returns on its two primary businesses of aggregates and RBB (roof tile unit)."
In 1996, sales fell back to 2.37 billion pounds versus 2.50 billion, with the total dividend payout frozen at 16.67 pence per share.

The poor result was blamed on sluggish European markets, particularly France and Germany which provides a major chunk of profits. But Redland also faced a strong sterling which ate into European revenues, wiping seven million off group operating profit.

The bad weather seen in Europe last year, which triggered a rash of downgrades across the sector, was the most damning factor, said Napier. That helped wipe 81 million stg off operating profits, despite a strong performance in North America.
